Applied.Outcome: Resolved with no reply: all twelve recommendations taken. Written into the plan under "Decided before the build".

Replies.Text:
Design, Step 1: Live Preview. Twelve decisions, each with my recommendation first. Resolve with no reply to take them all; reply with the numbers you want otherwise, and I apply the result under "Decided before the build".

1. The module. public/js/live-preview.js, an ES module beside anchormap.js, imported by codemirror-bundle.js and put on window.CodeMirror6.LivePreview: it needs the Lezer tree, Decoration and WidgetType, which a plain script has only through the bundle. It exports Extension( Options ), the extensions of the preview. In mirror.js, Create takes Options.Preview (on or off) and the instance gains SetPreview( On ), a Compartment reconfigured in place, so the toggle keeps the text, the cursor, the scroll and the undo history; the comment boxes (Plain) never take it.

2. The mechanism. A StateField of decorations over the whole document, rebuilt when the document changes or the revealed lines change (a selection moving within one line rebuilds nothing); not a ViewPlugin, because the table and image widgets are block decorations, which CodeMirror accepts from a field only. The tree comes from syntaxTree, with ensureSyntaxTree and a small time budget so a fresh document is parsed before it is drawn. The texts here are plan-sized; the rebuild is one walk of the tree.

3. The reveal rule. A line that any selection range touches shows its source; a fenced code block or a table shows its source whole when a range touches any of its lines. Everywhere else the rendering applies. A click into rendered text puts the cursor there and the line reveals, the text shifting by the width of its marks, as in Obsidian. No atomic ranges: the cursor never has to step over a hidden mark, since the line it is on has none hidden.

4. What each construct becomes off the cursor's line. Headings: the marks hidden (the # run and its space, a setext underline), the line in the Read view's heading sizes. Emphasis, strong, strikethrough: the marks hidden, the text styled as the highlight style already does. Inline code: the backticks hidden, monospace on the panel background. Links: text alone, in the accent and underlined, the URL and title hidden; Ctrl+click (Cmd on a Mac) opens the URL in a new tab, as the Read view's link does; a plain click edits. Autolinks as they are, styled as links. Bullet lists: the -, * or + replaced by a bullet, the indentation kept, so nesting reads; ordered lists keep their numbers. Task items: [ ] and [x] replaced by a checkbox that toggles the source on click (an edit, so Save lights up). Blockquotes: the > marks hidden, the lines with a left border and the muted colour. Fenced code: the fence lines hidden behind a thin label naming the language, the code lines monospace on the panel background, editable in place. Horizontal rules: the line replaced by a rule. Tables: the whole table replaced by a block widget holding marked's HTML of its lines, in the Read view's table styles; a click on the widget puts the cursor on the table's first line, which reveals the source. Images: ![alt](url) replaced by the image, the alt as its tooltip, the Read view's width limit; when it fails to load, the alt text. Escapes: the backslash hidden.

5. What stays as source in this cut: HTML blocks and tags, link reference definitions and the labels of reference links, entities, hard breaks (the two trailing spaces) and footnotes. Rare in plans; later if missed.

6. Typography. In Live Preview the editor takes the page's prose font and size (the Read view's); the line numbers and the fold gutter are gone, the active line keeps its faint background. Source mode is the editor as it is today: monospace, line numbers, fold gutter. The anchors' marks look the same in both.

7. The Source toggle in this step. A Source button in the edit bar, where the Preview button is in Monaco mode (id source-toggle, pressed when on). State.Source, remembered in the browser under source-mode, shared the way the Editor setting is; off by default, so the Live Preview is what opens. Step 3 moves it into the heading and gives it Ctrl+E.

8. The preview pane. In CodeMirror mode the Edit view is the editor alone: no preview pane, no splitter, no Preview button; the key preview-hidden-codemirror goes. Monaco mode keeps all three.

9. The anchors. Nothing changes: the field maps the plain positions through the anchor map, which knows nothing of what is hidden; a mark may span a hidden range; the mousedown on a mark still selects the thread; the marks stay off while the text differs from the saved one, as now.

10. Styles. The preview's classes (cm-live-h1 to h6, cm-live-code, cm-live-fence, cm-live-quote, cm-live-rule, cm-live-table, cm-live-image, cm-live-check) in edit-view.css, over the palette variables and the article's sizes, so the Read view and the preview read alike; the font switch, which the theme extension must make, in mirror.js.

11. Tests. The pure part is testable in node: live-preview.js exports Plan( Source, RevealedLines ), listing the decorations as ranges with their kinds, which the field turns into Decoration objects; test/LivePreview.test.js runs it over a fixture holding every construct, the way AnchorMap.test.js runs the map. Browser tests in Ui.test.js, CodeMirror mode: the heading's marks are absent from the DOM off the cursor's line and present on it; the Source toggle shows them all and the choice survives a reload; the checkbox click edits the text and lights Save; the table widget shows and a click on it reveals the source; an image renders; the two thread marks are still there; Save works. The smoke: CodeMirror opens in Live Preview with the Source button and the marks. The 187 node tests and Monaco's test path untouched.

12. Out of this step: the heading and the Read and Edit buttons (Step 3), the threads' functions in the editor (Step 2), the hotkeys (Step 3), the guide (Step 5).

Applied.Outcome: The build was accepted as reported (the smoke count corrected in the reply: 39); no text change. Committed as "Markdown Editor: Step 1".

Replies.Text:
Build log, Step 1: Live Preview. Built as decided, with the notes below; the Live Preview is in the CodeMirror editor, the Source button beside Save, the preview pane gone in CodeMirror mode, Monaco mode untouched. Resolve to have it committed as "Markdown Editor: Step 1"; reply where something should be otherwise.

What was done

1. public/js/live-preview.js, an ES module (decisions 1, 2, 11): Plan( Source, Revealed, Tree ) walks the Lezer tree and lists the decorations as ranges with kinds (line with its class, hide, bullet, check, link, code, fence-start, fence-end, setext, rule, table, image); Extension() is the state field that builds Decoration objects from the plan over the whole document, rebuilt when the document changes or the set of revealed lines changes (the key is the sorted line numbers), plus the Ctrl+click handler that opens a rendered link in a new tab. The tree is the editor's, finished with ensureSyntaxTree under a 100 ms budget; the node test parses with the anchor map's parser and gets the same plan.
2. The reveal rule (3): a line any selection range touches shows its source; a fenced code block or a table shows whole when a range touches any of its lines. Checked in the browser: the cursor's heading line shows its marks and the others do not; a click into a rendered heading reveals it; a click on the table widget puts the cursor on its first line and the source comes back.
3. The constructs (4, 5): headings (ATX with their closing marks, setext with its underline as a thin rule), emphasis, strong, strikethrough, inline code, links (text alone, the URL as the tooltip), autolinks, bullets, task checkboxes (a click toggles [ ] and [x] in the source, Save lights), blockquotes, fenced code (the fences as the top bar with the language and the bottom bar, the code lines editable on the panel background), horizontal rules, tables (marked's HTML of the lines, in the Read view's table styles), images (the image itself, the alt text when it does not load), escapes. HTML, entities, hard breaks, link references, reference links and footnotes stay as source. Indented code blocks get the code lines' background too.
4. Typography (6, 10): the Live Preview takes the page's font and size through the editor's theme, keyed on the editor class cm-live, and sits at the Read view's width, centred, with the room below; no line numbers or fold gutter (a compartment, empty in Live Preview). The styles are in edit-view.css under their own heading. Source mode is the editor as before.
5. The Source button (7): in the edit bar where Monaco's Preview button is, id source-toggle, pressed when on; State.Source, remembered under source-mode (shared, like the Editor setting), off by default; State.SetSource broadcasts source-changed. The switch reconfigures two compartments in place, so the text, the cursor, the scroll and the undo history stay.
6. The preview pane (8): in CodeMirror mode the edit body is the editor alone (the pane and the splitter are ng-if'd away, the grid is one column) and the preview is not rendered at all; the key preview-hidden-codemirror is gone, preview-hidden is Monaco's. Monaco mode is as it was.
7. The anchors (9): untouched; the two marks of the test plan are there in the Live Preview and in Source, follow an edit and are found again on save.
8. Tests (11): test/LivePreview.test.js, four tests over a fixture with every construct (the plan with nothing revealed, the ordering and the whole-line blocks and the non-overlapping replacements, the revealed lines and blocks, the tree given against the parser). Ui.test.js: the existing CodeMirror test now checks there is no preview pane or Preview button and that the editor opens as the Live Preview with the Source button; a new test drives the Live Preview end to end (the hidden and revealed heading, the bullets, the checkbox, the fence, the table, the image, the link, Source on and off and remembered, the checkbox edit saved with Ctrl+S, the marks found again, back to Monaco). node --test: 192 pass (187 before, 4 node tests and 1 browser test added). The smoke gained two checks on the page part (the Live Preview with the Source button and nothing of the preview; the bullets); the whole smoke (npm run smoke, the page and the desktop parts, on a temporary config and user data) ends SMOKE OK with 44 checks, 22 on the page and 22 in the desktop.

Notes and departures

- The editor class cm-live is set through the editorAttributes facet inside the preview compartment, not by toggling the class list: CodeMirror owns the editor element's class attribute and rewrote it on the first focus, which the first run of the browser tests found.
- The editor's markdown language is now markdown( { base: markdownLanguage } ), the GFM one: the plain CodeMirror language has no Table, TaskMarker or Strikethrough nodes, and the preview reads the editor's own tree. The comment boxes share the language, so they highlight GFM too; nothing else changes for them.
- The escape's backslash is a plain hide item, not a kind of its own: the plan lists eleven kinds, the design named twelve.
- The instance also got IsPreview(), for Step 3's heading button to read.
- A table widget and an image widget are block and inline replacements from the one field; a link's children are not walked, so an escaped character inside a link's text keeps its backslash (two replacements must not nest).
- The Monaco tests and the server tests ran untouched. Nothing of the guide, the help or the heading changed (Steps 3 and 5).

A correction to point 8: the smoke's count and its first run. The whole smoke was run twice. The first run passed the page part (20 checks, the two new ones among them) and stopped in the desktop part at the Escape that closes the Hotkeys popup, which did not close within ten seconds; a screenshot probe of mine was driving another browser at the same moment, and nothing of this step touches the popup or the key. The second run, alone, ended SMOKE OK with 39 checks, page and desktop. The log above says 44 checks; 39 is the number.
